state_and_units.s: stipulated signal contribution at receiver port, complex V peak
state_and_units.b: environmental witness-equivalent nuisance, complex V peak
state_and_units.y: reconstructed receiver effective voltage, complex V peak
state_and_units.w: calibrated witness-equivalent voltage, complex V peak; not automatically raw coil voltage
state_and_units.beta: complex dimensionless signal leakage into witness
state_and_units.epsilon_y,epsilon_w: supplied deterministic complex measurement-error radii, V
state_and_units.Delta_a: supplied complex transfer uncertainty radius, dimensionless

model.clean_witness: y=s+a b; w=b. Known a gives linear map [[1,a],[0,1]] over C² (four real dimensions) and s=y-a w.
model.without_witness: y only has real rank2, domain4, nullity2 with complex kernel(-a t,t), t in V.
model.deterministic_disk: |shat-s| ≤ epsilon_y+|ahat|epsilon_w+Delta_a(|what|+epsilon_w). Prove triangle inequality and test boundary fixtures; distinguish bound from confidence interval.
model.calibration_scope: The 2mV receiver error bound is a NEW stipulated effective-voltage bound, chosen slightly above the R2 nominal1.932mV scale. It is not derived for all R3 circuit conditions and must be separately calibrated physically. No real sensor performance is asserted.
model.unknown_transfer_rival: If a is unbounded, a'=a+δa and s'=s-δa b reproduce both y and w. For the nonzero fixture choose δa=s/b so s'=0. Domain(s,b,a) is C³=R⁶, local real rank4/nullity2; explicit tangent kernel(-b t,0,t), t dimensionless.
model.witness_crossleak: If w=b+beta s with known beta, matrix [[1,a],[beta,1]] has complex determinant1-a beta. Along beta=t/a report inversion/conditioning for t≠1. At t=1 provide exact kernel(-a u,u), u in V, and withhold unique inversion. Unknown beta is not assumed harmless.
model.physical_identity: Even with a clean known witness, s=s_exotic+d with unmonitored ordinary same-port drive d gives domain(s_exotic,d,b)=C³=R⁶, rank4/nullity2 and exact kernel(t,-t,0), t in V. Save finite pair with all5mV assigned to s_exotic versus all to d and identical y,w.
model.boundary: Effective single-frequency linear transfer model only. No stochastic noise/search statistics, geometric axion coupling, electromagnetic field solve, thermal mechanics, gravity law or actual environmental observations.

controls: Clean exact witness recovers injected complex5mV signal
Zero stipulated signal with background alone subtracts to zero for known exact transfer
512 boundary cases: eight phases each for receiver error, witness error and transfer error; report inclusion, not probability
Construct one aligned error fixture attaining the data-dependent bound within tolerance
Unknown a admits exact zero-signal rival matching BOTH readouts
Real ranks/domain/nullities and explicit kernels for no witness, clean known witness, unknowna local map, singular crossleak and expanded source-identity map
Near-singular crossleak path: determinant, rank and condition; singularpoint returns no unique inverse
Remaining physical-source identity exact rival survives perfect witness subtraction

acceptance.positive_control: Nominal5mV signal disk excludes zero under statedcleanwitness/calibration assumptions; otherwise reportfailurewithoutretuning.

artifacts: CSV uncertainty/crosstalk paths and exact rivals
Deterministic SVG uncertainty and conditioning plots
record.falsifier: Failure of the predicted calibrated subtraction or bound rejects this implementation. An exact ordinary rival blocks an exotic-source interpretation even if a nonzero effective signal remains.
limits: Witness calibration and stationarity must be measured; sensor blindness to the signal is an assumption to test
Known crosstalk can be inverted only away from its singular boundary
No real apparatus, dark-matter sensitivity, free-energy extraction or gravity modification is established
Three authorized rounds end here; future physical tests are roadmap items, not hidden extra loops
record.next_round_rule: No further research round is authorized in this program. R3B selects physical calibration and source-discrimination obligations for the roadmap; finalize three rounds/six loops and stop numerical expansion.

terms.label: Peak amplitude
terms.plain: Peak amplitude is the largest excursion from zero.
terms.meaning: The imported R1/R2/R3 electrical phasors use peak amplitude, while the host circuit inputs use RMS.
cautions: Sample peak, reconstructed true peak and acoustic pressure peak are different measurements.

terms.label: Phase and coherent readout
terms.plain: Phase locates one repeating signal relative to another.
terms.meaning: Coherent complex readout preserves relative amplitude and phase under a declared shared reference.
cautions: Sharing a sample clock does not establish equal gain, stable transfer or calibration.

terms.label: Calibration and deterministic error bounds
terms.plain: Calibration connects instrument readings with a stated reference.
terms.meaning: These contracts supply deterministic error radii in volts, amperes, henries or dimensionless transfer units, as declared.
cautions: A stipulated error radius is not measured sensor performance or a confidence interval.

terms.label: Not to scale
terms.plain: A sketch may show relationships without preserving size ratios.
terms.meaning: Use written dimensions and declared coordinate units rather than measuring screen pixels.
cautions: An accurate-looking diagram is not an engineering drawing or a calibrated photograph.

terms.label: Imaginary unit
terms.plain: The imaginary unit represents a quarter-turn in complex arithmetic.
terms.meaning: j² = −1; imported contracts often write i instead. It is not electrical current i(t).
cautions: Interpret i from its equation context, not from its character alone.

terms.label: Phasor
terms.plain: A phasor combines a sinusoid’s size and phase into one complex number.
terms.meaning: It represents a single-frequency sinusoid under an explicitly selected peak or RMS convention.
cautions: A phasor is not an instantaneous waveform or automatically a physical electromagnetic field.

terms.label: Complex and real-number domains
terms.plain: A complex number has a real and an imaginary part.
terms.meaning: Two complex source values have four real coordinates: ℂ² is represented by ℝ⁴.
cautions: ℂ is not capacitance C; ℝ is not electrical resistance R.

terms.label: Real part, imaginary part and conjugate
terms.unit: same unit as the complex quantity
terms.plain: These operations separate or reverse parts of a complex number.
terms.meaning: For z = a + jb, Re(z)=a, Im(z)=b and conjugate(z)=a−jb.
cautions: The a and b here are generic coordinates, not automatically witness transfer parameters.

terms.label: Magnitude and squared magnitude
terms.unit: signal unit; its square for squared magnitude
terms.plain: Magnitude measures the size of a complex quantity without its phase.
terms.meaning: For z=a+jb, |z|²=a²+b²; measuring magnitude discards phase information.
cautions: A² is squared amperes here; it is not a new kind of current.

terms.label: Estimate, difference and time derivative
terms.plain: Marks over a symbol tell you which version, change or bound is meant.
terms.meaning: A hat denotes an estimate; δ often a difference or perturbation; Δ can denote a final-minus-initial change or a supplied error bound, according to the contract; a dot is a time derivative.
cautions: Δa and ΔM in these contracts are error-bound radii, not temporal changes. Every symbol needs declared units; ż is velocity, not position.

terms.label: Matrix, transpose, diagonal and inverse
terms.plain: A matrix collects several linked equations into one map.
terms.meaning: Transpose T swaps rows/columns; diag forms a diagonal matrix; inverse undoes an invertible map.
cautions: A matrix inverse is not defined at a singular parameter choice.

terms.label: Rank, nullity and kernel
terms.unit: counts of real or complex dimensions, explicitly declared
terms.plain: Some different inputs can produce exactly the same observations.
terms.meaning: Rank counts independent observed directions; nullity counts unobserved directions; a kernel vector maps to zero.
cautions: State whether dimensions are real or complex. A nonzero kernel defeats unique reconstruction.

terms.label: Determinant and conditioning
terms.unit: depends on matrix units; dimensionless for witness map
terms.plain: A determinant can reveal when a square map cannot be inverted.
terms.meaning: The witness map is singular when 1−aβ=0; conditioning describes sensitivity near inversion.
cautions: A small numerical residual is not a guarantee of stable physical inference.

terms.label: Signal and nuisance contributions
terms.plain: The receiver can mix the intended signal with ordinary background.
terms.meaning: s is a stipulated receiver signal, b a witness-equivalent nuisance and y their combined effective receiver voltage.
cautions: A recovered same-port signal is not automatically an exotic physical source.

terms.label: Calibrated witness-equivalent voltage
terms.plain: A witness channel observes a declared background reference.
terms.meaning: The variable w is a calibrated equivalent voltage, not automatically the raw pickup-coil voltage.
cautions: w is not work; a label W on a recorder identifies its role, not watts.

terms.label: Nuisance transfer
terms.plain: Transfer tells how the background enters the receiver.
terms.meaning: a maps witness-equivalent nuisance voltage into receiver effective voltage at one selected frequency.
cautions: Geometry alone does not calibrate a; unknown transfer can preserve rival explanations.

terms.label: Transfer uncertainty radius
terms.plain: The contract places a bound on how much the transfer ratio may be wrong.
terms.meaning: Δa bounds the magnitude of the difference between true and estimated complex nuisance transfer.
cautions: It is not a voltage or a final-minus-initial time change; the bound is supplied, not measured here.

terms.label: Signal leakage into the witness
terms.plain: A reference channel can accidentally contain the signal too.
terms.meaning: β maps the intended receiver signal into the witness channel.
cautions: This β is not a pressure-reflection coefficient or a statistical error probability.

terms.label: Deterministic reconstruction disk
terms.plain: The stated assumptions bound the reconstruction inside a disk.
terms.meaning: Triangle inequalities propagate supplied complex error radii into a worst-case voltage radius.
cautions: A deterministic bound is not a confidence interval or evidence of a new force.

terms.label: Numerical sample and grid counts
terms.plain: A grid count says how many numerical evaluations were requested.
terms.meaning: These are computational sampling choices, not counts of physical measurements or participants.
cautions: More grid points do not themselves establish model accuracy or experimental replication.

terms.label: Dimensionless witness-leakage path
terms.plain: This parameter moves along a family of leakage settings.
terms.meaning: In the R3 conditioning probe, β=t/a so aβ=t. At t=1 the witness map is singular.
cautions: This t is not elapsed time in seconds or the acoustic path delay.

terms.label: SI and unit prefixes
terms.plain: SI is the international system of measurement units.
terms.meaning: cm=0.01 m, mm=0.001 m, µ=10⁻⁶, milli=10⁻³ and nano=10⁻⁹ of the stated unit.
cautions: A source drawing in cm or mm is not silently a metres-based parts table.

terms.label: Scalable Vector Graphics
terms.plain: SVG stores a drawing as shapes and text.
terms.meaning: A vector drawing can retain dimensions and annotations independently of display resolution.
cautions: A precise-looking SVG is not a validated construction drawing.

terms.label: JavaScript Object Notation
terms.plain: JSON stores structured data that can be exported and inspected.
terms.meaning: A receipt encodes declared inputs, outputs and provenance as text records.
cautions: Serialization does not authenticate a claim or measure a device.

terms.label: SHA-256 content digest
terms.plain: A digest helps compare whether two files have the same bytes.
terms.meaning: SHA means Secure Hash Algorithm; the digest identifies content under the named algorithm.
cautions: A matching digest proves neither the truth of content nor its author.

equations.title: A witness needs a known transfer
equations.plain: Subtracting background works only under the declared transfer and leakage assumptions.
equations.convention: Complex peak effective voltages at one frequency; a and β dimensionless.
equations.units: s,b,y,w V; a,β dimensionless; error radii V.
cautions: At aβ=1 the map is singular. A separated same-port contribution is not a uniquely identified exotic source.

handbook.title: Environmental witness and signal leakage
handbook.overview: An independently read pickup and calibrated complex transfer test whether ordinary background can be separated from a receiver-port residual.
handbook.goal: Ask whether an extra observation can help separate an assumed signal from ordinary background without giving the residual a new physical identity.
signalSteps: The receiver observation contains a stipulated signal plus transferred background.
The witness channel is a second measurement related to that background after calibration.
Subtract the calibrated background contribution while carrying the stated measurement and transfer errors.
Check whether signal leakage into the witness or an alternative ordinary source can reproduce the same observations.

terms.label: Peak amplitude
terms.plain: Peak amplitude is the largest excursion from zero.
terms.meaning: The imported R1/R2/R3 electrical phasors use peak amplitude, while the host circuit inputs use RMS.
cautions: Sample peak, reconstructed true peak and acoustic pressure peak are different measurements.

terms.label: Phase and coherent readout
terms.plain: Phase locates one repeating signal relative to another.
terms.meaning: Coherent complex readout preserves relative amplitude and phase under a declared shared reference.
cautions: Sharing a sample clock does not establish equal gain, stable transfer or calibration.

terms.label: Calibration and deterministic error bounds
terms.plain: Calibration connects instrument readings with a stated reference.
terms.meaning: These contracts supply deterministic error radii in volts, amperes, henries or dimensionless transfer units, as declared.
cautions: A stipulated error radius is not measured sensor performance or a confidence interval.

terms.label: Not to scale
terms.plain: A sketch may show relationships without preserving size ratios.
terms.meaning: Use written dimensions and declared coordinate units rather than measuring screen pixels.
cautions: An accurate-looking diagram is not an engineering drawing or a calibrated photograph.

terms.label: Imaginary unit
terms.plain: The imaginary unit represents a quarter-turn in complex arithmetic.
terms.meaning: j² = −1; imported contracts often write i instead. It is not electrical current i(t).
cautions: Interpret i from its equation context, not from its character alone.

terms.label: Phasor
terms.plain: A phasor combines a sinusoid’s size and phase into one complex number.
terms.meaning: It represents a single-frequency sinusoid under an explicitly selected peak or RMS convention.
cautions: A phasor is not an instantaneous waveform or automatically a physical electromagnetic field.

terms.label: Complex and real-number domains
terms.plain: A complex number has a real and an imaginary part.
terms.meaning: Two complex source values have four real coordinates: ℂ² is represented by ℝ⁴.
cautions: ℂ is not capacitance C; ℝ is not electrical resistance R.

terms.label: Real part, imaginary part and conjugate
terms.unit: same unit as the complex quantity
terms.plain: These operations separate or reverse parts of a complex number.
terms.meaning: For z = a + jb, Re(z)=a, Im(z)=b and conjugate(z)=a−jb.
cautions: The a and b here are generic coordinates, not automatically witness transfer parameters.

terms.label: Magnitude and squared magnitude
terms.unit: signal unit; its square for squared magnitude
terms.plain: Magnitude measures the size of a complex quantity without its phase.
terms.meaning: For z=a+jb, |z|²=a²+b²; measuring magnitude discards phase information.
cautions: A² is squared amperes here; it is not a new kind of current.

terms.label: Estimate, difference and time derivative
terms.plain: Marks over a symbol tell you which version, change or bound is meant.
terms.meaning: A hat denotes an estimate; δ often a difference or perturbation; Δ can denote a final-minus-initial change or a supplied error bound, according to the contract; a dot is a time derivative.
cautions: Δa and ΔM in these contracts are error-bound radii, not temporal changes. Every symbol needs declared units; ż is velocity, not position.

terms.label: Matrix, transpose, diagonal and inverse
terms.plain: A matrix collects several linked equations into one map.
terms.meaning: Transpose T swaps rows/columns; diag forms a diagonal matrix; inverse undoes an invertible map.
cautions: A matrix inverse is not defined at a singular parameter choice.

terms.label: Rank, nullity and kernel
terms.unit: counts of real or complex dimensions, explicitly declared
terms.plain: Some different inputs can produce exactly the same observations.
terms.meaning: Rank counts independent observed directions; nullity counts unobserved directions; a kernel vector maps to zero.
cautions: State whether dimensions are real or complex. A nonzero kernel defeats unique reconstruction.

terms.label: Determinant and conditioning
terms.unit: depends on matrix units; dimensionless for witness map
terms.plain: A determinant can reveal when a square map cannot be inverted.
terms.meaning: The witness map is singular when 1−aβ=0; conditioning describes sensitivity near inversion.
cautions: A small numerical residual is not a guarantee of stable physical inference.

terms.label: Signal and nuisance contributions
terms.plain: The receiver can mix the intended signal with ordinary background.
terms.meaning: s is a stipulated receiver signal, b a witness-equivalent nuisance and y their combined effective receiver voltage.
cautions: A recovered same-port signal is not automatically an exotic physical source.

terms.label: Calibrated witness-equivalent voltage
terms.plain: A witness channel observes a declared background reference.
terms.meaning: The variable w is a calibrated equivalent voltage, not automatically the raw pickup-coil voltage.
cautions: w is not work; a label W on a recorder identifies its role, not watts.

terms.label: Nuisance transfer
terms.plain: Transfer tells how the background enters the receiver.
terms.meaning: a maps witness-equivalent nuisance voltage into receiver effective voltage at one selected frequency.
cautions: Geometry alone does not calibrate a; unknown transfer can preserve rival explanations.

terms.label: Transfer uncertainty radius
terms.plain: The contract places a bound on how much the transfer ratio may be wrong.
terms.meaning: Δa bounds the magnitude of the difference between true and estimated complex nuisance transfer.
cautions: It is not a voltage or a final-minus-initial time change; the bound is supplied, not measured here.
